title: 2020 AMC 10B Problem 5
statement: How many distinguishable arrangements are there of \(1\) brown tile, \(1\) purple tile, \(2\) green tiles, and \(3\) yellow tiles in a row from left to right? (Tiles of the same color are indistinguishable.)

solutions.text:
There are \(1+1+2+3=7\) total tiles. If all seven tiles were distinct, there would be \(7!\) arrangements. The two green tiles are indistinguishable, and the three yellow tiles are indistinguishable, so we divide by \(2!\) and \(3!.\)

Thus the number of arrangements is \[\frac{7!}{2!3!}=420.\]

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: First arrange the seven tiles as if they were all different
Divide by the orders of the identical green and yellow tiles
